# CH Calls Data Flow

How clonal hematopoiesis variant calls move between the MRD work and the cohort work. The concept behind it, CH as noise in one study and exposure in the other, is in [[clonal-hematopoiesis]]; this note is about plumbing.

## One caller, two consumers

- The caller lives in the [[clonal-hematopoiesis-filter]] repository, owned by [[hannah-lindqvist]]. It runs on buffy coat or white-cell sequencing and outputs all candidate variants at VAF 0.5% or more with flags.
- MRD use: calls from matched buffy coat are subtracted from cfDNA calls before MRD scoring. Threshold and filters are tuned to remove every plausible CH variant.
- Cohort use: calls from Northvale buffy coat are frozen as [[ch-subcohort-variant-calls]] and summarised per person for the [[ch-cancer-risk-analysis]]. The CH definition (2% primary) is applied at analysis time.

## Rules

- No forks. If the cohort analysis needs a different option, Hannah adds it upstream and both projects record the caller version they used.
- Frozen releases carry the caller version and container digest; re-running with a newer caller creates a new release, never an overwrite.
- Shared panel-of-normals resources are versioned in the filter repository.

## Why it matters

When the MRD filter improved in 2026 (better germline removal), the cohort calls did not silently change. Lucas will decide whether to re-call before the paper, and both results will be traceable.
